title: Nimbus overview
text: Nimbus is a cloud backup and file sync service for small teams. It keeps a versioned copy of every watched folder and lets a member restore any earlier version from the web console. Nimbus runs a background agent on each device that watches folders and uploads changes. The agent is named the Nimbus Relay. The Relay batches changes and uploads them every ninety seconds by default, which keeps network use low on slow links. A team can lower that interval in the console for faster sync. Nimbus stores data in regional buckets. A workspace is pinned to one region when it is created and the region cannot be changed later without a full migration handled by support.

title: Nimbus pricing and plans
text: Nimbus offers three plans. The Free plan includes five gigabytes of storage and keeps thirty days of version history. The Team plan includes one terabyte of storage per member and keeps one year of version history. The Business plan adds unlimited version history and priority restore. Billing is monthly or annual. Annual billing gives a discount of two months. The Team plan costs twelve dollars per member each month on monthly billing. A plan change takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle, and a downgrade never deletes data, it only hides versions older than the new retention window until an upgrade restores access to them.

title: Runbook: restore a deleted file
text: This runbook explains how to restore a file that a member deleted. Deletion in Nimbus is soft, so a deleted file moves to the Trash and is kept there before it is purged. Open the web console and go to the Trash view for the workspace. Search for the file by name or by the member who deleted it. Select the file and choose Restore to return it to its original folder. Trash keeps deleted files for thirty days before a permanent purge. After the purge a file can only be recovered from a version snapshot if one exists. An administrator can extend the Trash window to ninety days on the Business plan.

title: Runbook: resolve a sync conflict
text: A sync conflict happens when two devices edit the same file before either upload completes. Nimbus never silently discards an edit. When the Relay detects a conflict it keeps both versions. The original name is kept for the version that reached the server first. The second version is saved beside it with the suffix conflicted copy and the device name. A member then compares the two files and merges them by hand, then deletes the conflicted copy. To reduce conflicts, keep the sync interval low and avoid editing the same document on two offline devices at once.

title: Nimbus security model
text: Nimbus encrypts data in transit with modern transport security and encrypts stored data at rest. Each workspace holds its own data key. Server side encryption at rest uses the AES two fifty six cipher. Keys are rotated by the platform on a schedule and a workspace owner can trigger an immediate rotation from the security page. A rotation re-encrypts new writes and does not require a download of existing data. Nimbus supports single sign on for the Team and Business plans. Access logs record every restore and every export and are kept for one year.

title: API reference: authentication
text: The Nimbus API uses bearer tokens. A workspace owner creates a token on the developer page and scopes it to read only or read write. Send the token in the Authorization header on every request. A token that is unused for ninety days is revoked automatically. The API rejects a revoked or expired token with the status code 401 and a short error body. Rate limits apply per token. The default limit is six hundred requests per minute and a request over the limit returns the status code 429 with a retry after header that tells the caller how many seconds to wait.

title: API reference: files endpoint
text: The files endpoint lists, uploads, and downloads files in a workspace. A list request returns a page of file records with an id, a path, a size, and a version number. Upload uses a two step flow. First the caller requests an upload ticket, then the caller puts the bytes to the ticket url. An upload larger than one hundred megabytes must be sent in parts, and each part except the last must be at least five megabytes. A download request returns a short lived url that expires after ten minutes. The url is single use and a second download needs a fresh request.

title: Install the Nimbus Relay agent
text: The Relay agent runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Download the installer for the platform from the downloads page and sign in with a workspace invite. On macOS the agent needs Full Disk Access granted in system settings before it can watch protected folders. On Linux the agent is shipped as a single static binary and is managed by a user service unit. After install, the agent shows a tray icon. A green icon means sync is healthy. An amber icon means the agent is paused or waiting on a conflict. The agent log is written to the application data folder and is useful for a support ticket.

title: Version history and retention
text: Nimbus keeps a version each time a watched file changes and the Relay uploads the change. Versions are deduplicated at the block level, so a small edit to a large file stores only the changed blocks. Retention depends on the plan. The Free plan keeps thirty days, the Team plan keeps one year, and the Business plan keeps versions forever. A version older than the retention window is removed during a nightly cleanup. Pinning protects a version from cleanup. A member pins an important version from the file history panel, and a pinned version is kept regardless of the plan retention window until the member removes the pin.

title: Share a folder with a link
text: A member shares a folder by creating a share link from the console. A link can be view only or allow upload. A share link can carry an expiry date and an optional passcode. A link without an expiry stays active until a member revokes it. Revoking a link is immediate and breaks every copy of that link. External people who open a view only link can download files but cannot see the version history of the folder. Upload links let an external person add files to a drop folder without seeing anything already inside it.

title: Notifications and alerts
text: Nimbus sends notifications for restores, for share link use, and for storage that is near the plan limit. A member sets the channel in profile settings. The default channel is email. A workspace on the Business plan can also send alerts to a chat webhook. A storage alert fires when usage passes ninety percent of the plan limit so a team can act before uploads start to fail. Notifications are best effort and are not a substitute for the access log. The access log is the system of record for who restored or exported a file.

title: Nimbus mobile app
text: The Nimbus mobile app shows recent files and lets a member restore a version from a phone. The app does not run a full folder sync, it is a viewer and a light editor. Automatic camera upload is available on the mobile app. When it is on, new photos upload to a dedicated Camera folder in the workspace on a charger and on wifi by default. A member can allow upload on cellular in the app settings. The mobile app signs out after thirty days of no use and asks for the account passcode or a device biometric on each launch for extra safety.

title: Administrator roles
text: A Nimbus workspace has three roles. A Member can sync, restore, and share their own folders. An Administrator can manage members and shared folders. An Owner has every administrator power and also controls billing and the region. Only an Owner can delete the workspace or change the plan. There is exactly one Owner, and ownership is transferred from the security page after the new owner confirms by email. An Administrator cannot see the file contents of another member unless that member shares a folder with them. Role changes are written to the access log.

title: Storage limits and overage
text: Each plan sets a storage limit. When a workspace reaches the limit, new uploads are blocked but existing files stay available and sync continues for deletes and downloads. A storage alert fires at ninety percent of the limit. At one hundred percent, the Relay pauses uploads and shows an amber tray icon on every device. A team clears the block by deleting files, by emptying the Trash, or by upgrading the plan. Deleting a file does not free space until the Trash is emptied and any pinned versions of the file are unpinned, because a pinned version keeps its blocks.

title: Migrate a workspace to a new region
text: A workspace is pinned to one region at creation. Moving it to a new region is a migration that only Nimbus support can run, because it copies every block across regions and then repoints the workspace. A migration is planned for a quiet window. During the copy the workspace stays readable but new uploads are paused. The cutover itself takes a few minutes, and the Relay on each device reconnects to the new region automatically. A migration does not change any share link or any API token. It does reset the short lived download urls, so a script that cached a download url must request a fresh one after the cutover.

title: Troubleshoot: sync is stuck
text: If sync is stuck, first check the tray icon. An amber icon points at a paused agent, a conflict, or a full workspace. Open the agent and read the status line. If it says waiting on conflict, open the conflict runbook and resolve the conflicted copy. If it says storage full, clear space or upgrade. If it says the token expired, sign in again from the agent. A restart of the Relay agent clears most transient stalls. On Linux restart the user service unit. If a single file never uploads, it may exceed the plan file size cap, which is five gigabytes on the Team plan.

title: Export workspace data
text: An Owner or Administrator can export a full copy of workspace data from the console. The export is a set of archive files that mirror the folder tree. An export runs in the background and the console emails a download link when it is ready. The link follows the same short lived rule as the API and expires after ten minutes, so start the download promptly. An export includes the current version of every file. It does not include older versions or the Trash. Every export is written to the access log with the member who ran it and the time it finished.

title: Work offline with Nimbus
text: The Relay agent keeps working while a device is offline. Edits are saved locally and queued, and the queue uploads when the device reconnects. A folder can be marked available offline so its files are always kept on the device. Other folders are kept as online only placeholders that download on first open, which saves disk space on a small drive. Two devices that edit the same file while both are offline will create a sync conflict when they reconnect, so the conflict runbook applies after a long offline period on more than one device.

title: Webhooks for workspace events
text: Nimbus can post a webhook for workspace events such as a restore, a share link creation, and a storage alert. Webhooks are a Business plan feature. An Owner registers a webhook url on the developer page and selects the events to send. Nimbus signs each webhook with a secret so the receiver can verify that the call came from Nimbus and not from a forged source. A webhook that fails is retried with backoff for up to one hour. After that the event is dropped and only the access log keeps the record.

title: Account recovery
text: A member who loses access recovers the account by email. Nimbus sends a sign in link that is valid for fifteen minutes to the address on file. If the member also lost access to the email address, only an Owner or Administrator can help by removing the old member and sending a fresh invite, which keeps the folders the member had shared with the team. Nimbus does not store a recoverable password, so support cannot read or reset a password to a known value. Recovery always goes through an email sign in link or an administrator reinvite.
